Chédiak-Higashi neutrophils contain few giant fused granules rather than numerous coarse toxic granules.
Promyelocytes have azurophilic granules but a round nucleus with fine chromatin, unlike this mature segmented nucleus.

2046.recognize_zh: 背景為多顆染色質粗塊狀的小淋巴球；兩個箭頭指向較大的淋巴細胞，細胞質較多、染色質較不緻密，代表 CLL 中混雜的較大細胞（疑似 prolymphocyte）；左下有一顆被壓碎的細胞（smudge cell）。
features: Background of small lymphocytes with coarsely clumped chromatin and scant cytoplasm
Arrowed cells are larger lymphoid cells with more abundant pale blue cytoplasm and less condensed chromatin
Nucleoli not sharply resolved in the arrowed cells at this image quality
Irregular crushed lymphoid nucleus (smudge-type cell) at lower left
Normal neutrophil and a granulated mononuclear cell with folded nucleus for size comparison
Red cells normocytic without significant abnormality
2046.describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows numerous small lymphocytes with coarsely clumped chromatin and scant cytoplasm. Admixed are larger lymphoid cells (arrows) with more abundant pale cytoplasm and somewhat less condensed chromatin; distinct central nucleoli are not clearly resolved at this resolution. A crushed smudge-type cell, a neutrophil and a granulated mononuclear cell are also present. Findings are consistent with chronic lymphocytic leukemia with admixed larger cells; if prolymphocytes are confirmed, their proportion should be quantified.

ddx.dx: B-prolymphocytic leukemia / CLL with increased prolymphocytes
ddx.vs: Prolymphocytic disease is defined by a predominance of medium-sized cells with a prominent central nucleolus, not a minority of larger cells among block-chromatin small lymphocytes.
MCL shows more pleomorphic, irregular nuclei and requires CD23, CD200 and cyclin D1/SOX11 testing to exclude.

ddx.dx: Reactive large granular or atypical lymphocytes
ddx.vs: Reactive lymphocytes have abundant cytoplasm that hugs adjacent red cells or contains azurophilic granules and occur without a monotonous small-lymphocyte background.

1982.recognize_zh: 組織切片中血管/竇腔內擠滿鮮紅色、細長鐮刀狀的紅血球（粗箭頭指出一團緊密堆積的鐮狀細胞，細箭頭指單一鐮狀細胞），間質細胞稀少、造血前驅細胞不多，符合鐮狀細胞病中紅血球鐮變淤塞的表現。
features: Numerous elongated, crescent- and needle-shaped sickled red cells within vascular/sinusoidal spaces and stroma
Thick arrow: tightly packed aggregate of sickled cells occluding a vessel (vaso-occlusion)
Thin arrow: individual sickle cell
Large empty rounded spaces separated by thin cellular septa
Sparse nucleated cells (small lymphocytes, plasmacytoid and stromal/endothelial cells) without obvious active hematopoiesis in this field
1982.describe_en: Section shows large rounded empty spaces separated by thin septa that contain sparse nucleated cells and abundant sickled erythrocytes. Vascular channels are distended and packed with aggregates of elongated sickle-shaped red cells (thick arrow), and individual sickle forms are scattered in the stroma (thin arrow). Active hematopoietic precursors, including the giant pronormoblasts of parvovirus B19 infection, are not evident in this field; tissue site cannot be determined with certainty from this image. Findings are consistent with sickle cell disease with in situ sickling and vaso-occlusion, compatible with a hypocellular marrow in the setting of aplastic crisis.

ddx.vs: SC disease shows fewer classic elongated sickle cells and more target cells and blunt, crystal-containing (SC) cells.

ddx.dx: Postmortem or fixation-induced sickling in sickle trait
ddx.vs: Artifactual in vitro sickling can occur in HbAS tissue, so vaso-occlusion must be correlated with hemoglobin electrophoresis and the clinical picture.
Aplastic anemia shows marrow hypocellularity without sickled cells, whereas aplastic crisis in SCD is transient red cell aplasia due to parvovirus B19 with giant pronormoblasts.

1662.recognize_zh: 周邊血液中一顆比紅血球大約兩倍的細胞，核呈摺疊、分葉狀（像腎形扭曲），染色質鬆散略成網狀，細胞質豐富呈灰藍色、帶細小顆粒——這是正常單核球的典型外觀。
features: Large cell, about twice the diameter of surrounding red cells
Folded, lobulated (irregular kidney-shaped) nucleus
Loosely clumped, lacy chromatin without nucleoli
Abundant grey-blue cytoplasm with fine dust-like granules
Background normocytic red cells without significant poikilocytosis
1662.describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a single large mononuclear cell with a folded, lobulated nucleus, loosely clumped chromatin without nucleoli, and abundant grey-blue cytoplasm containing fine granules. The surrounding red cells are normocytic and normochromic. Findings are consistent with a normal mature monocyte.

ddx.vs: Reactive lymphocytes have clearer, more basophilic cytoplasm that scallops around red cells and a rounder nucleus without lobulation.
Promonocytes have finer, more open chromatin, sometimes nucleoli, and are counted as blast equivalents, unlike the mature chromatin here.
Neutrophil precursors have pink-lilac cytoplasm with specific granules and denser chromatin rather than grey-blue cytoplasm.

60926.recognize_zh: 大細胞的卵圓核中間有一條細緻摺痕（delicately folded），染色質細而開放，外圍是大量淡灰藍色細胞質帶細嗜天青顆粒與小空泡，是前單核球（promonocyte）的樣貌。
features: Large cell, about 2.5 times the diameter of adjacent red cells, with an irregular cytoplasmic border
Oval nucleus with a delicate longitudinal fold/crease
Finely granular, open chromatin, less condensed than a mature monocyte; nucleolus not clearly visible
Abundant pale grey-blue cytoplasm with fine azurophilic granules
Several small cytoplasmic vacuoles beneath the nucleus
60926.describe_en: High-power smear shows a large mononuclear cell with abundant pale grey-blue cytoplasm containing fine azurophilic granules and several small vacuoles. The nucleus is oval with a delicate longitudinal fold, and the chromatin is finely dispersed and more open than that of a mature monocyte; nucleoli are not conspicuous. No Auer rods are identified. Findings are consistent with a promonocyte, a blast equivalent in the classification of monocytic neoplasms.

ddx.vs: Mature monocytes have coarser, condensed chromatin with deeper nuclear lobulation.
Monoblasts have round nuclei with prominent nucleoli and more basophilic cytoplasm without nuclear folding.
Histiocytes are larger with more abundant, often phagocytic cytoplasm and oval nuclei with finely vesicular chromatin, usually seen in tissue or aspirate rather than blood.

126.recognize_zh: 周邊血液抹片同時看到正常色素紅血球與小球性低色素紅血球（雙相性，dimorphic），分析儀 RBC 直方圖也呈雙峰；骨髓 Perls 鐵染色可見藍色鐵顆粒環繞紅血球母細胞核一圈（環狀鐵粒幼細胞，ring sideroblasts），且骨髓鐵儲存增加。
features: Dimorphic red cell population: normochromic cells admixed with microcytic hypochromic cells
Marked anisopoikilocytosis with dacryocytes, elongated/pencil forms, fragments and occasional target cells
Analyzer RBC histogram with two populations and 'Dimorphic Reds' flag; MCV 68.7 fL, RDW 35.1%
Perls stain of aspirate: coarse blue siderotic granules arranged around erythroblast nuclei (ring sideroblasts)
Abundant stainable iron in marrow particles (increased iron stores)
Cellular aspirate with maturing granulocytes and erythroid precursors; no blasts increase evident
126.describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows marked anisopoikilocytosis with a dimorphic red cell population composed of normochromic red cells and microcytic hypochromic cells, accompanied by dacryocytes, elongated forms, fragments and occasional target cells. The automated analyzer RBC histogram shows two red cell populations with a 'Dimorphic Reds' flag, low MCV (68.7 fL) and very high RDW (35.1%), and platelet histogram interference at the upper end. The bone marrow aspirate is cellular with maturing granulocytic and erythroid elements. Prussian blue (Perls) stain shows increased iron in marrow particles and erythroblasts with coarse perinuclear siderotic granules forming rings. Findings are consistent with congenital sideroblastic anemia, in keeping with the X-linked (ALAS2) type in this male child with iron overload.

ddx.vs: Also microcytic hypochromic, but marrow stainable iron is absent and ring sideroblasts are not seen, whereas here iron stores are increased with ring sideroblasts.
Microcytosis with target cells and nucleated red cells, but HbA2/HbF are abnormal on HPLC and ring sideroblasts are not a feature; HPLC was normal here.
Shows ring sideroblasts but typically macrocytic/dimorphic in older adults with dysplasia in other lineages and SF3B1 mutation, not infantile-onset microcytic anemia.

ddx.dx: Acquired sideroblastic anemia (alcohol, copper deficiency, isoniazid, zinc toxicity)
ddx.vs: Morphologically similar ring sideroblasts; separated by exposure history, copper/zinc levels and reversibility rather than by morphology.

captions: Peripheral blood: dimorphic red cells with hypochromic microcytes, dacryocytes and fragments
Analyzer printout: bimodal RBC histogram with 'Dimorphic Reds' flag, MCV 68.7 fL, RDW 35.1%
Bone marrow aspirate (Wright-Giemsa): cellular smear with maturing myeloid and erythroid precursors
Perls stain, low power: marrow particle with abundant stainable iron
Perls stain, high power: erythroblasts with perinuclear ring of siderotic granules (ring sideroblasts)

62.recognize_zh: 低倍下淋巴結被寬厚的膠原纖維帶切割成多個結節，結節內散布許多周圍有空隙的大細胞（腔隙細胞，lacunar cells）；免疫染色中大細胞呈 CD30 膜狀加高基氏體點狀陽性、CD15 點狀陽性、PAX5 弱陽性，符合結節硬化型典型何杰金淋巴瘤。
features: Lymph node architecture effaced by broad collagen bands dividing the parenchyma into cellular nodules
Numerous lacunar Hodgkin/Reed-Sternberg (HRS) cells: large cells with abundant clear to retracted cytoplasm sitting in clear spaces, multilobated nuclei and prominent nucleoli
Occasional mononuclear HRS variants and a dense, deeply eosinophilic 'mummified' cell
Mixed inflammatory background of small lymphocytes, eosinophils, plasma cells and histiocytes
HRS cells: CD30 membranous and Golgi (paranuclear dot) positive, CD15 paranuclear/granular positive, PAX5 weak nuclear versus strong in background B cells
Scattered small background lymphocytes positive for a membranous marker while the large atypical cells are negative
62.describe_en: Sections of the excised cervical lymph node show effacement of the architecture by a nodular process in which broad collagen bands surround cellular nodules. The nodules contain numerous large lacunar-type Hodgkin/Reed-Sternberg cells with retracted clear cytoplasm, multilobated nuclei and prominent nucleoli, together with occasional mummified cells, in a background of small lymphocytes, eosinophils, plasma cells and histiocytes. By immunohistochemistry, the large cells are positive for CD30 (membranous and Golgi pattern) and CD15 (paranuclear dot/granular), and show weak PAX5 compared with strongly positive background B cells; they are negative for the membranous marker that highlights scattered small reactive lymphocytes. Findings are consistent with classical Hodgkin lymphoma, nodular sclerosis subtype.

ddx.vs: LP 'popcorn' cells lack lacunar retraction and sclerotic bands, are CD20+ with strong PAX5, and are CD30-/CD15-, unlike the CD30+/CD15+/PAX5-weak lacunar cells here.
ALCL forms cohesive sheets of hallmark cells with uniform strong CD30, frequent T-cell antigen/cytotoxic marker expression, and PAX5 negativity rather than the weak PAX5 of HRS cells.

ddx.dx: Primary mediastinal (thymic) large B-cell lymphoma / mediastinal gray zone lymphoma
ddx.vs: PMBL shows sheets of large cells with strong CD20, CD79a and OCT2/BOB1 and preserved B-cell program, whereas HRS cells here are scattered and have a downregulated B-cell program.
Large cells are CD20+/strong PAX5 and CD30-/CD15- in a background of T cells and histiocytes, lacking eosinophil-rich infiltrate and fibrous nodules.

62.stain: H&E; IHC: CD30, CD15, PAX5, membranous lymphoid marker
captions: Low power: broad fibrous bands divide the node into cellular nodules (H&E)
Nodule edge with collagen band and numerous lacunar cells (H&E)
Clusters of lacunar HRS cells with clear retracted cytoplasm among small lymphocytes (H&E)
High power: lacunar cells with multilobated nuclei and prominent nucleoli (H&E)
Mixed background with eosinophils, histiocytes and a mummified cell (H&E)
Membranous IHC highlights scattered small lymphocytes; central large atypical cell is negative (likely CD20/CD3)
PAX5: strong in background B cells, weak nuclear staining in large HRS cells
CD30: membranous and Golgi-pattern staining of HRS/lacunar cells
CD15: paranuclear dot and granular cytoplasmic staining in HRS cells

60862.recognize_zh: CD20 染色下可見一個以膜型陽性 B 細胞密集構成的結節狀聚集，邊緣向周圍疏鬆組織散出成群陽性細胞，上方有少數較大的陽性細胞；配合臨床，這是邊緣區淋巴瘤（marginal zone lymphoma）中 B 細胞結節性浸潤的表現。
features: Dense nodular aggregate of CD20-positive small B cells with crisp membranous staining
Small clusters and single CD20-positive cells extending into the surrounding loose stroma
Occasional larger CD20-positive cells at the top of the aggregate
Adjacent loose, edematous/adipose-like stroma with CD20-negative background
No distinct germinal center or mantle zone architecture discernible on this stain
60862.describe_en: Immunohistochemical stain for CD20 highlights a dense nodular aggregate of small B cells with strong membranous staining, with small clusters and single B cells extending into the surrounding loose stroma. Occasional larger CD20-positive cells are present at the upper aspect of the nodule. Cytologic detail (monocytoid or plasmacytoid features, lymphoepithelial lesions) is not assessable on this stain. In conjunction with H&E morphology, light chain restriction, and a CD5-/CD10-/cyclin D1-negative profile, findings are consistent with involvement by marginal zone lymphoma.

ddx.vs: Reactive follicles show a germinal center with CD10/BCL6-positive, BCL2-negative cells and polytypic plasma cells, whereas marginal zone lymphoma shows expanded B-cell areas with light chain restriction.
Follicular lymphoma nodules are CD10/BCL6 positive with BCL2 co-expression in follicle centers and t(14;18).
Mantle cell lymphoma is CD5 and cyclin D1/SOX11 positive, whereas marginal zone lymphoma is negative for both.
CLL/SLL co-expresses CD5, CD23, and LEF1 and shows proliferation centers.

1214.recognize_zh: 周邊血液中有數顆小至中型淋巴球，染色質凝集，細胞質中等量淡藍，其中一顆細胞邊緣有細小不規則突起（可能為極性絨毛），並可見紅血球內有 Howell-Jolly 小體；配合臨床，這是脾邊緣區淋巴瘤（splenic marginal zone lymphoma）的白血病期表現。
features: Small to medium-sized lymphocytes with round nuclei and condensed, clumped chromatin
Moderate rim of pale blue cytoplasm; one cell with subtle irregular, short cytoplasmic projections
Nucleoli inconspicuous
Two normal segmented neutrophils and scattered platelets
Red cells with Howell-Jolly bodies in the lower left, suggesting hyposplenism or prior splenectomy
1214.describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows several small to medium-sized lymphocytes with round nuclei, condensed chromatin, inconspicuous nucleoli, and moderate pale blue cytoplasm; one cell shows subtle short irregular cytoplasmic projections, although classic polar villi are not clearly demonstrated. Segmented neutrophils and platelets appear normal, and a few red cells contain Howell-Jolly bodies, raising the possibility of hyposplenism or prior splenectomy. The morphology is not specific on its own. In conjunction with splenomegaly and flow cytometry showing a CD5-/CD10-/CD103- light chain-restricted B-cell population, findings are consistent with leukemic splenic marginal zone lymphoma.

ddx.vs: Hairy cells have circumferential fine hair-like projections and bean-shaped nuclei, with CD103/CD25/CD11c positivity, annexin A1, and BRAF V600E.
CLL cells have scant cytoplasm, soccer-ball chromatin, and smudge cells, and co-express CD5 and CD23.
Cells often have irregular nuclear contours and are CD5 and cyclin D1/SOX11 positive.
Shows plasmacytoid lymphocytes with an IgM paraprotein and MYD88 L265P mutation.

4222.recognize_zh: 尿液沉渣以 Perls 普魯士藍染色，可見成團的深藍色含鐵血黃素（hemosiderin）顆粒聚集，背景為粉紅色；這是慢性血管內溶血（如 PNH）的尿含鐵血黃素陽性表現。
features: Clusters of coarse, deep blue Prussian blue-positive granules (hemosiderin), likely within shed renal tubular cells
Two discrete aggregates plus scattered isolated blue granules
Pink nuclear fast red counterstained background with amorphous debris and occasional non-staining crystals
No intact red cells evident in this field
4222.describe_en: Cytocentrifuged urine sediment stained with Perls Prussian blue shows aggregates of coarse, dark blue iron-positive granules consistent with hemosiderin, most likely contained within desquamated renal tubular epithelial cells, together with scattered free blue granules. The background contains amorphous pink debris and occasional refractile crystals, which are iron-negative. Findings indicate hemosiderinuria, consistent with chronic intravascular hemolysis as seen in paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria.

ddx.vs: Hematuria shows intact red cells and a positive dipstick but lacks Prussian blue-positive granules unless hemolysis has been chronic.
Myoglobinuria gives a heme-positive dipstick without hemosiderin-laden tubular cells, and serum CK is markedly elevated.
Precipitate and bacteria are refractile or basophilic on routine stain but do not show the granular blue iron reaction confined to cell-shaped aggregates.
